def bracket_wrap_each(items):
    """Hey — quick formatting helper needed for our little tag-style display.

    The setup couldn't be simpler: items is a list of strings. We want each
    one turned into a bracketed chunk and all the chunks glued straight
    together, back to back. To spell it out exactly: Return the items each
    wrapped in square brackets and concatenated with nothing between them,
    e.g. '[a][b]'; return the empty string for empty items.

    That's genuinely the whole job — no separators, no spaces, no trimming,
    no surprises. Brackets around each string, everything jammed together,
    and an empty result when there's nothing to wrap. Should be a one-liner
    if you feel like it, but any approach works.

    >>> bracket_wrap_each([])
    ''
    >>> bracket_wrap_each(['a'])
    '[a]'
    """
